title: Ссора у Вики и сломанный реквизит  (The Fight at Vika's and Broken Equipment)

segments.t: Jealous after seeing Igor leave, Max confronts Vika in her apartment and accuses her of having an affair with Igor, infuriating her. Meanwhile at the restaurant, Chef Barinov and Nagiyev get drunk and smash Barani's imported kitchen equipment.
Виктория Сергеевна, вы ради бога извините нас.
Я расстроился, что не смог его купить.
В общем, мы так расстроились, что немножко перебрали.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Are you out of your mind?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'to oneself'.
'Between you and Igor.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'by' and 'you' in a few short words. Vika answers right away.
'Just like I saw with my own eyes.' In Russian, the idea of 'how' flows naturally into 'saw' without extra filler words.
'Well, what else could I think?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'to think'.
'Max, you are the one who needs a doctor.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'Max' and finishing on 'needed'. Vika answers right away.
'So you two were playing doctor?' Notice how Russian expresses 'so that' and 'to play' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Виктория Сергеевна, вы ради бога извините нас.
'Viktoriya Sergeyevna, for goodness' sake forgive us.' Max anchors the line on 'Viktoriya', while 'us' completes the thought.
'Dima just got upset.' The grammar packs 'Dima' and 'got upset' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Vika answers right away.
Я расстроился, что не смог его купить.
'I got upset that I could not buy it.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'should I buy?' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
В общем, мы так расстроились, что немножко перебрали.
'Anyway, we got so upset that we drank a little too much.' Notice how Russian expresses 'short' and 'drank too much' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'And at yourself.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'both' and finishing on 'yourself'. Vika answers right away.
'Do not stress about it.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'not' in a few short words.
'Wonderful, just marvelous.' The meaning hinges on 'wonderful' working together with 'wonderful' in spoken Russian. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
